verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              राजन् कुरूणां प्रवरैर्बलैर्भीममभिद्रुतम् । मज्जन्तमिव कौन्तेयमुज्जिहीर्षर्धनञ्जयः ॥१॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said O monarch, Dhananjaya, seeing, Bhima almost sinking under the pressure of the attack of many of great Kaurava warriors, left aside the son of Suta and his division, O Bharata and went to the rescue of his brother and sent many warriors of the hostile army to Pluto's region.

verses.sanskrit: विमृद्य सूतपुत्रस्य सेनां भारत सायकैः । प्राहिणोन्मृत्युलोकाय परवीरान् धनञ्जयः ॥२॥
ततोऽस्याम्बरमाश्रित्य शरजालानि भागशः । अदृश्यन्त तथाऽन्ये च निजघ्नुस्तव वाहिनीम् ॥३॥
verses.english: His showers of shafts fell dividedly, some covered the skies, while other killed your army.

verses.sanskrit: स पक्षिसंघाचरितमाकाशं पूरयञ्शरैः । धनञ्जयो महाबाहुः कुरूणामन्तकोऽभवत् ॥४॥
verses.english: O king, Dhananjaya, filling the sky (which is the place for birds to play) with his arrows, seemed at that time the very destroyer of Kurus.

verses.sanskrit: ततो भल्लैः क्षुरप्रैश्च नाराचैर्विमलैरपि । गात्राणि प्राच्छिनत्पार्थः शिरांसि च चकर्त ह ॥५॥
verses.english: He with his long flat-pointed shafts and various other brilliant weapons and keen like razor, began to cut-off bodies and heads of enemies.

verses.sanskrit: छिन्नगात्रैर्विकवचैर्विशिरस्कैः समन्ततः । पातितैश्च पतद्भिश्च योधैरासीत्समावृता ॥६॥
verses.english: Warriors dead and dying, trunks without heads, lopped off portions of human bodies deprived of armour, covered the battle-field.

verses.sanskrit: धनञ्जयशराभ्यस्तैः स्यन्दनाश्वरथाद्विपैः । संछिन्नभिन्नाविध्वस्तैर्व्यङ्गाङ्गावयवैः स्तृता ॥७॥
verses.english: O monarch, heaps of unshapely and mangled bodies of elephants and horses, cutoff by Dhananjaya with his weapons in different ways and broken cars made the field look ghastly and awful and the way uneven and impassable, resembling the great river Vaitarani.

verses.sanskrit: सुदुर्गमा सुविषमा घोराऽत्यर्थं सुदुर्दृशा । रणभूमिरभूद्राजन्महावैतरणी यथा ॥८॥
ईषाचक्राक्षभल्लैश्च व्यश्वैः साश्वैश्च युध्यताम् । ससूतैर्हतसूतैश्च रथैस्तीर्णाऽभवन्मही ॥९॥
verses.english: It was also strewn with cars, some without horses and some with horses yoked on them and some with drivers and some without drivers, as also with broken axles, wheels and arrows.

verses.sanskrit: सुवर्णवर्णसन्नाहैर्योधैः कनकभूषणैः । आस्थिताः क्लृप्तवर्माणो भद्रा नित्यमदा द्विपाः ॥१०॥
verses.english: Four hundred fearful and highly trained elephants ridden by wrathful warriors enveloped in golden coloured armors and decked with golden ornaments, urged by the pressure of the heels and toes of their guides, who were also powerful, filled with rage and cruel, came forward and was struck down by the chosen weapons of Kiritin or the diademdecked Arjuna and fell down resembling great mountain tops inhabited by living beings when loosened. Dhananjaya covered the earth by killing many great and choice elephants by his shafts.

verses.sanskrit: क्रुद्धाः क्रूरैर्महामात्रैः पार्ष्ण्यङ्गुष्ठप्रचोदिताः । चतुःशताः शरवरैर्हताः पेतुः किरीटिना ॥११॥
पर्यस्तानीव शृङ्गाणि समृद्धानि महागिरेः । धनञ्जयशराभ्यस्तैः स्तीर्णा भूर्वरवारणैः ॥१२॥
समन्ताज्जलदप्रख्यान्वारणान्मदवर्षिणः । अभिपेदेऽर्जुनरथो घनान् भिन्दन्निवांशुमान् ॥१३॥
verses.english: Heaps of carcasses of elephants with greasy matter oozing out of them looked like clouds and as the sun stands out in relief dispersing the clouds, so Dhananjaya's car passed through these masses of dead elephants.

verses.sanskrit: हतैर्गजमनुष्याश्वैर्भिन्नैश्च बहुधा रथैः । विशस्त्रयन्त्रकवचैर्युद्धशौण्डैर्गतासुभिः ॥१४॥
verses.english: Phalguna made a great havoc and the path was covered with dead horses, men, elephants and with many broken chariots, as also with dead bodies of warriors divested to their coats of mail, instruments of war and other weapons and the place was also strewn over with various sorts of weapons loosened from the clutches that held them.

verses.sanskrit: अपविद्धायुधैर्मार्गः स्तीर्णोऽभूत्फाल्गुनेन वै । व्यस्फारयद्वै गाण्डीवं सुमहद्भैरवारवम् ॥१५॥
verses.english: The awful sound made by his out-stretched Gandiva was like the clash of thunder amidst the gloomy clouds.

verses.sanskrit: घोरवज्रविनिष्पेषं स्तनयित्नुरिवाम्बरे । ततः प्रादीर्यत चमूर्धनञ्जयशराहता ॥१६॥
महावातसमाविद्धा महानौरिव सागर । नानारूपाः प्राणहराः शरा गाण्डीवचोदिताः ॥१७॥
verses.english: As in a hurricane a great vessel is wrecked to pieces by the tossing of the sea, so your army was broken and it suffered badly from Dhananjaya's shots.

verses.sanskrit: अलातोल्काशनिप्रख्यास्तव सैन्यं विनिर्दहन् । महागिरौ वेणुवनं निशि प्रज्वलितं यथा ॥१८॥
verses.english: Lots of deadly, burning and meteor-like shots, coming like thunder-bolts out of the Gandiva, began to burn down your troops.

verses.sanskrit: तथा तव महासैन्यं प्रास्फुरच्छरपीडितम् । संपिष्टदग्धविध्वस्तं तव सैन्यं किरीटिना ॥१९॥
verses.english: As on a night, a blazing forest of bamboos burns on a great mountain, so your great army looked ablaze under fire from (Arjuna's) shots.

verses.sanskrit: कृतं प्रविहतं बाणैः सर्वतः प्रद्रुतं दिशः । महावने मृगगणा दावाग्नित्रासता यथा ॥२०॥
verses.english: Your troops, being thus hard pressed, burnt and distressed and killed by Kiritin's (Arjuna's), arrows began to fly in all directions.

verses.sanskrit: कुरवः पर्यवर्तन्त निर्दग्धाः सव्यसाचिना । उत्सृज्य च महाबाहुं भीमसेनं तथा रणे ॥२१॥
verses.english: As in a great forest, herds of deer being afraid fly wildly in all directions when it catches fire, verily such became the fate of the Kauravas when they were burnt to death by Savyasachin.

verses.sanskrit: बलं कुरूणामुद्विग्नं सर्वमासीत्पराङ्मुखम् । ततः कुरुषु भग्नेषु बीभत्सुरपराजितः ॥२२॥
verses.english: Leaving the strong-armed Bhimasena the distressed Kaurava troops retreated from the filed.

verses.sanskrit: भीमसेनं समासाद्य मुहूर्तं सोऽभ्यवर्तत । समागम्य च भीमेन मन्त्रयित्वा च फाल्गुनः ॥२३॥
verses.english: Thus breaking down the Kuru army the unconquerable Vibhatsu then approached Bhimasena and resied there for a while.

verses.sanskrit: विशल्यमरुजं चास्मै कथयित्वा युधिष्ठिरम् । भीमसेनाभ्यनुज्ञातस्ततः प्रायाद्धनञ्जयः ॥२४॥
verses.english: Phalguna then receiving Bhima's caress and consulting him for a while, informed him that the arrows with which Yudhishthira was afflicted have been drawn out of his body and that he is keeping well.

verses.sanskrit: नादयन् रथघोषेण पृथिवीं द्यां च भारत । ततः परिवृतो वीरैर्दशभिर्योधपुङ्गवैः ॥२५॥
verses.english: O Bharata, then taking Bhima's permission, Dhananjaya again advanced towards his enemies, making the earth and sky ring back with the rattling noise of his car-wheels.

verses.sanskrit: दुःशासनादवरजैस्तव पुत्रैर्धनञ्जयः । ते तमभ्यर्दयन्बाणैरुल्काभिरिव कुञ्जरम् ॥२६॥
verses.english: Then your ten sons, who were born after Dushasana, all good warriors and brave hearted, surrounded Dhananjaya.

verses.sanskrit: आततेष्वसनाः शूरा नृत्यन्त इव भारत । अपसव्यांस्तु तांश्चक्रे रथेन मधुसूदनः ॥२७॥
verses.english: O Bharata, they with drawn bows distressed Arjuna with fiery arrows even as do the hunters an elephant and seemed to dance in the battlefield (With excitement).

verses.sanskrit: नियुक्तान्हि स तान्मेने यमायाशु किरीटिना । ततस्ते प्राद्रवञ्शूराः पराङ्मुखरथेऽर्जुने ॥२८॥
verses.english: And the destroyer of (Asura) Madhu, quite confident that Kiritin will soon send them to the region of Pluto, urged on the car, brought them all to the right side.

verses.sanskrit: तेषामापततां केतूनश्वांश्चापानि सायकान् । नाराचैरर्धचन्द्रैश्च क्षिप्रं पार्थो न्यपातयत् ॥२९॥
verses.english: Then seeing that Arjuna with his car was getting from them, they made a rush towards him. Then Partha soon struck off their banners, bows and horses and they fell down on the earth; then with some crescent-shaped arrows.

verses.sanskrit: अथान्यैर्दशभिर्भल्लैः शिरांस्येषामपातयत् । रोषसंरक्तनेत्राणि संद‌ष्टौष्ठानि भूतले ॥३०॥
verses.english: And with ten other shafts cut-off their heads. Those heads with lips and eyes red with rage looked fair like a collection of lotuses.

verses.sanskrit: तानि वक्त्राणि विबभुः कमलानीव भूरिशः । तांस्तु भल्लैर्महावेगैर्दशभिर्दश कौरवान् ॥३१॥
रुक्माङ्गदान् रुक्मपुङ्खैर्हत्वा प्रायाद‌मित्रहा ॥३२॥
